name: Finasteride
lead: Finasteride is an oral inhibitor of the type II and III isoforms of 5-alpha-reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Approved at 1 mg daily as Propecia for male pattern hair loss and at 5 mg as Proscar for benign prostatic hyperplasia, it is the most established medical treatment for slowing androgenetic alopecia.

In trials most men maintain or regrow some hair over several years, with the benefit lost within months of stopping. It is a cornerstone of hair-loss protocols in looksmaxxing and hair-loss communities, usually paired with minoxidil.

paras: Hair loss in androgenetic alopecia is driven by DHT acting on genetically sensitive scalp follicles, which shrink and spend less time in the growth phase. Finasteride lowers serum DHT by roughly 70 percent and scalp DHT by a similar amount, reducing miniaturisation and allowing some follicles to recover.

Decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and ejaculatory problems occur in a minority, and depression and anxiety have been reported. Some men describe persistent sexual or mood symptoms after stopping (post-finasteride syndrome), a condition regulators have noted but whose frequency and cause remain debated. It can affect PSA readings, is contraindicated in pregnancy because of fetal risk, and women should not handle crushed tablets. It is prescription-only.
